data.narrative:
Wayve, a Series D autonomous systems company founded by Amar Shah and Alex Kendall, commands a current post-money valuation of $8.6B on $1.5B raised. The company operates within the Drones & Autonomous sector, evaluated against a peer set of 4 same-sector comparables including Zipline ($7.6B Series G), Joby Aviation ($6.9B public), Nuro ($6.0B Series G), and Archer Aviation ($3.3B public), with valuations ranging from $3.3B to $7.6B.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using a typical 1.5x Series D step-up multiplier, implies a forward valuation of $12.9B. Peer-median analysis across the four-company set yields $6.4B, reflecting the current market consensus for similarly-positioned autonomous technology players. These approaches produce substantial divergence, reflecting uncertainty about Wayve's positioning relative to both earlier-stage comparable companies and the maturity profile of public-market comparables.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $5.5B (low) to $14.8B (high), with a median of $9.7B. The $8.6B current valuation sits slightly below this median, suggesting modest upside under base-case assumptions. Key uncertainties include the appropriate stage-to-stage multiplier for Series D in this sector and whether peer valuations reflect sustainable market economics or speculative positioning in autonomous vehicle segments.
